title: Goldman and Apollo Market Slices of Record $40B SpaceX GPU Financing

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The private equity firm and the investment bank have begun offering Wall Street investors portions of a GPU debt package designed to fund SpaceX's artificial intelligence hardware acquisitions. Goldman Sachs and Apollo are marketing these slices, some as large as $500 million, to institutional buyers ahead of a formal syndication process. The funding includes an $8.3 billion senior-secured loan and multiple bond tranches rated from BBB to A-, structured so that the debt remains off SpaceX's balance sheet to maintain its credit ratings.

The financing will facilitate the purchase of $47.3 billion in Nvidia hardware, primarily next-generation Rubin chips, funded by $40 billion in debt and a $7 billion prepayment from SpaceX. The hardware is slated for delivery in the first half of 2027. Under the five-year lease, SpaceX's payment obligations are unconditional, meaning the company must continue payments regardless of equipment damage or operational disruptions.

The arrangement is a key component of Apollo's strategy to secure control of $75 billion in AI chips through agreements with SpaceX and Anthropic. Once finalized, the stockpile would make the private equity giant a larger hardware owner than any specialized AI cloud provider, trailing only the major hyperscale cloud companies.

selectedTweets.text:
Goldman Sachs $GS and Apollo $APO are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX $SPCX's roughly $40B AI chip financing deal.

The two firms have begun marketing the financing to potential buyers, with some investors being offered portions worth as much as $500M ahead of the formal syndication process, which is expected to begin soon.

The financing, announced in October, is the largest GPU financing arrangement on record.

Here's how the deal is structured:

An Apollo-backed entity will purchase approximately $47.3B worth of Nvidia GPUs and related equipment, primarily its next-generation Rubin chips.

The purchases will be financed through roughly $40B in debt, alongside a $7B lease prepayment from SpaceX.

SpaceX will then lease the chips for approximately five years, using a structure designed to keep the financing debt off its own balance sheet and protect its credit ratings.

The debt package includes an $8.3B senior-secured loan, alongside multiple bond tranches being marketed to institutional investors.

The Nvidia chips are expected to be delivered in the first half of 2027.

One interesting detail is that SpaceX's rental obligations remain unconditional.

The company must continue making payments even if the equipment is damaged or extraordinary events disrupt operations. SpaceX also isn't providing a guarantee covering the chips' residual value at the end of the lease.

Source: Bloomberg
